thread:
support-alex: FYI escalation from AcmeCorp. They report p99 on /v1/generate doubled overnight (~1200ms -> ~2600ms). Customer says billing spike and timeouts for some calls. They reproduced with 50 concurrent streams. Attached snippet they used to repro and a link to their logs: https://acmecorp.logs/xyz :point_down:

support-alex: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-small","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":200}'
```

sre-bot: deploy: release/metrics-lib v2.1.0 -> prod by jules at 2026-03-18T01:58:12Z :rocket:

maria: Thanks Alex. I'm looking at our prod dashboards. The p99-series (api.prod:/v1/generate p99) does show a step at ~02:00 UTC. But the histogram panel for the same route doesn't show the same magnitude. One is using our histogram rollup metric (ingest.histogram_seconds) while the other is using direct request_latencies bucketed by client->panel. That could explain the mismatch.

rob: Could also be bucket boundary change. I remember a metrics-lib PR changed how we compute bucket upper bounds (rounding behaviour) — PR #432? If those buckets shifted, quantiles computed from histograms can move non-smoothly.

jules: That PR landed in the 01:58 deploy (yep, that was my deploy). It included a small change to histogram bucket normalization to reduce double-counting. I didn't expect it to shift the p99 that much.

ingrid: @jules any chance that the change caused histogram buckets to be reinterpreted in our rollup job? The rollup mapper reads the bucket label and groups by boundary value. If normalization changed boundaries (e.g., 1.999 -> 2.0), that can move a lot of samples between buckets.

maria: Exactly. I ran a quick comparison across two days with a query: ```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",env="prod"}[5m])) by (le))
```
and then vs the rollup series: ```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(ingest.histogram_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",env="prod"}[5m])) by (le))
```
The two diverge at 02:00. The raw buckets show a subtle shift in counts from the 2s bucket into the 4s bucket after normalization.

support-alex: Acme also provided traces — their top traces show retries and long tail on token streaming. They said a small subset of requests (0.2%) hit >6s. That lines up with the p99 jump.

rob: Two paths: rollback metrics-lib to restore previous bucket semantics (fast, clear mitigation), or patch dashboards/alerts to compute p99 against the new rollup semantics (safer long-term). For customer-facing SLA, we should rollback until we verify the new semantics.

product-lin: For customers, the metric change causing visible latency regression is bad. Even if actual service latency didn't change, perception matters. Recommend rollback + a small postmortem note to customers explaining metric change.

jules: Rolling back now. Triggering canary rollback to 3 nodes at 02:30 UTC, will promote if green. I'll post logs.

sre-bot: action: rollback start for release/metrics-lib at 2026-03-18T02:31:08Z by jules

maria: While that's running, lets add a short-term dashboard panel that uses the raw request_latency histogram (non-rollup) to confirm real latency. If raw doesn't show spike, then it's only metrics semantics.

jules: Rollback to metrics-lib v2.0.7 promoted at 02:39:42Z. Canary passed on 3 nodes. Promoting to full cluster now.

sre-bot: deploy: rollback/metrics-lib v2.0.7 -> prod completed at 2026-03-18T02:40:18Z :white_check_mark:

maria: I can confirm rollup and panel re-aligned after rollback. p99 returned to baseline within two 5m windows. Looks like this was a metrics-bucket semantics issue, not a serving regression.

support-alex: I'll tell AcmeCorp that we've mitigated and we're following up. They asked for repro instructions for the bug; can we provide a minimal repro and timeline?

rob: Minimal repro: run high QPS (50 concurrent) against /v1/generate for ~10 minutes before and after deploying the normalization change. Observe histogram buckets with `sum(rate(...bucket[5m])) by (le)` and watch how counts shift across boundaries. I can put a short gist with commands.

rob: gist: https://gist.github.com/rob/histogram-repro (will update with scrapes and queries)

ingrid: Long-term fixes: 1) Add unit tests that assert stable bucket labels when running normalization transforms. 2) Add a migration step that emits both old and new bucket naming for a week for back-compat. 3) Expand docs for dashboard authors to prefer either raw or rollup consistently.

product-lin: Also update the change log and notify customers on next status update. Add an alert for large p99 divergence between raw and rollup (e.g., >30% relative) so this can be flagged before customers notice.

jules: Filed follow-ups: GH issues #1745 (unit tests for histogram code), #1746 (dual-output migration path), #1747 (dashboard alert for rollup vs raw divergence). I'll own #1745 and #1746.

maria: Quick note on dashboards: Some panels used `increase()` on rollup counters which interacts poorly with bucket boundaries across scrape windows. Where possible prefer `rate()` + `histogram_quantile` on stable bucket series. I'll audit top-10 customer-facing panels.

support-alex: AcmeCorp responded: "Thanks — appreciate the quick rollback. Please share repro + timeline". I'll post the gist and the timestamps.

rob: Action items summary: 
- rollback completed (jules)
- send customer timeline & repro (support-alex + rob)
- add unit test + dual emit (jules + ingrid)
- dashboard audit of top-10 panels (maria)
- alert rule for raw vs rollup divergence (maria)

jules: I'll attach the deploy logs here: https://deploys.redwood.example/metrics-lib/rollbacks/1824005123/logs.txt

maria: Closing note: this is a useful reminder that observability changes are effectively customer-facing changes. Reverting when customer impact is perceived is the right call. :+1:

support-alex: I'll update AcmeCorp and mark the support ticket as resolved once customer confirms. Thanks all. :heart:
